title: Red Sea event-risk broadens as Saudi Arabia prepares anti-Houthi offensive
net_new_delta: Reuters reports Saudi Arabia is preparing an offensive, expected within weeks, involving more than 100,000 Yemeni ground forces with Saudi air support to regain control of the Bab el-Mandeb strait. This creates a distinct prospective Red Sea shipping/energy event-risk channel beyond the already-active Iran/China refined-product shock.

evidence.finding: Saudi Arabia is preparing an offensive against Iran-backed Houthis to regain control of Bab el-Mandeb; Reuters reports >100,000 Yemeni ground forces are expected to participate with Saudi air support, and launch is expected within weeks.

Brent settled at $102.25/bbl and WTI at $91.11/bbl after European countries agreed to release diesel reserves; China has suspended October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, preserving existing refined-product tightness.

assumptions_affected: Middle East energy risk can be represented primarily by crude supply/Hormuz variables
Red Sea shipping risk is secondary to existing Iran-war energy channels
conflicts: Emergency reserve releases are currently suppressing crude/diesel prices even as prospective Red Sea military escalation risk rises.
unknown: Whether the offensive launches on the reported timetable
Magnitude/duration of Bab el-Mandeb shipping disruption
Resulting freight, insurance, refined-product and inflation pass-through
next_decisive_check: Confirm actual mobilization/launch and test whether Red Sea freight/shipping disruption and refined-product cracks re-widen despite emergency reserve releases; absent operational confirmation, do not promote this from event-risk to realized supply shock.

oracle.finding: Add a time-valid RED_SEA_ESCALATION_RISK hypothesis separate from realized energy-supply shock; require operational confirmation before raising realized inflation/supply-disruption state.

supermesh_x.finding: Route Red Sea military/shipping evidence separately from crude price and refined-product evidence; Reuters provides fresh event-risk evidence, while reserve-release price action supplies an independent counter-signal.
